To: Renters Board / Notices
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT FOR REVIEW — Stop using Brightline Pro 6% batch LX2291

URGENT — please check your developer before your next colour client.

Kelvin Trade have confirmed a filling error with Brightline Pro 6% (20 vol) Cream Developer, 1L. Bottles from batch LX2291 may actually contain 12% (40 vol). That is double the strength on the label. This is a safety issue, not just an inconvenience.

STOP USING BATCH LX2291 IMMEDIATELY.

How to check yours

Check the BASE OF EACH BOTTLE for LX2291. The batch is not on the box, so checking the packaging alone will not do.

Check every bottle: the open ones in your trolley as well as unopened stock in the back. The affected batch was supplied between 19 October and 5 November 2026. Even if you cannot remember when you bought yours, check the bottle.

Put affected bottles aside, clearly marked “DO NOT USE”, away from working stock. If the code is missing or unreadable, leave that bottle out of use until Kelvin Trade can confirm it. Do not try to work out the strength by smell, appearance, a patch test or trying it on hair. Do not dilute it and carry on.

Kelvin Trade’s email says other batches and other strengths are not affected.

What has happened, and what to watch for

On Saturday I used a newly opened bottle marked 6%, batch LX2291, for a bleach retouch. The lift was much faster than usual and the client developed burning and red patches on the scalp. I stopped and rinsed immediately. No client details are being shared here.

There has also been a report here of the same batch lifting unusually fast with foils getting very hot. Please do not assume unexpected heat is just the heater.

Stronger developer than expected can make the colour or bleach process faster and more aggressively. That can mean unexpected lift, uneven results, dryness, damage and breakage, as well as scalp irritation or chemical burns. Extra heat, burning or unexpectedly fast lift are reasons to stop, not leave it another few minutes. You cannot confirm a bottle’s strength from how the hair looks.

If someone reacts in the chair

Stop the service immediately. Do not carry on processing or add toner to try to fix the result.

For a suspected chemical burn, call 999 for medical help immediately. Do not wait for blistering or severe pain. Follow the call handler’s instructions.

Protect yourself with gloves. Carefully remove contaminated clothing if possible and rinse the affected area with plenty of cool or lukewarm running water for about ONE HOUR. Do not delay rinsing while sorting phone calls or paperwork; get someone else to call if possible.

Do not use shampoo, creams, aloe or other chemicals on the affected area. Do not try to neutralise it. Chemical burns need hospital assessment. Breathing difficulty, throat swelling or collapse also mean 999 immediately.

This follows the NHS chemical-burn guidance linked in our “Patch tests and skin tests” page. A normal patch-test result does not make a mislabelled bottle safe.

Returns and keeping evidence

The Kelvin Trade rep is in on Tuesday 10 November. Affected bottles can go back to him or to the Hillington depot for a full credit.

If you have had a problem with a bottle, KEEP THAT BOTTLE BACK — do not bin it or hand your only evidence back with the routine returns. Keep it safely sealed and labelled out of use, with the batch visible, and arrange with the supplier how it will be retained or collected.

Record any incident in the incident book at the desk. Keep dated notes, product and batch details, processing times, the supplier email and, with the client’s consent, dated photos securely. Keep client names and photos off the board.

Please check your own stock today and make sure anyone else buying from the rep has seen this.

Kirsty
